newsitem.title: UK: Hanson reports first-half profit gain.
newsitem.headline: Hanson reports first-half profit gain.

text.p: Materials and services group Hanson Plc, which inherited the name of the once-mighty conglomerate that completed its split-up earlier this year, said Thursday it had pro-forma half-year pretax profits of 47.8 million pounds ($75.8 million).

"The rate of improvement in operating profit showed an increasing trend in the June quarter and Hanson is now moving forward in accordance with its long-term plan," Chairman Lord Hanson said in a statement accompanying the results.

Pro-forma operating profits for the six months to June 30, 1997 rose 9 percent to 121 million pounds ($192 million). The pretax profit figure of 47.8 million was derived after the company took a charge of 49 million ($78 million), which included a 28 million ($44 million) loss on the sale of Hanson Electrical.

Hanson said the company's U.S. interests were helped by the strength of the U.S. economy. It said the recovery was increasing in its British companies, although it noted this recovery had flattened in recent weeks.
The company warned that the British government's recent cancellation of a number of road projects and delays to others would affect its ARC building materials unit.
The pound's meteoric rise on the foreign exchanges hit the company's translation of European and foreign earnings by 4.4 million pounds ($6.9 million) at the profit level.
Hanson's U.S. shares slipped 12.5 cents to $25.625 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
